skill.name: azure-diagnostics
skill.description: Diagnose Azure production issues with structured guidance for App Service, Container Apps, Functions, AKS, Event Hubs, and Service Bus. Use Azure Monitor, resource health, AppLens, KQL, and safe CLI examples to collect evidence and plan remediation.
skill.summary: Guide Azure incident triage with service-specific diagnostics, evidence collection, and remediation planning.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: The static findings are documentation patterns, placeholders, or read-only diagnostic examples, and I did not confirm them as malicious code. A semantic issue remains because SKILL.md uses authority and mandatory-compliance wording that can interfere with instruction hierarchy.

remediation.suggestion: Remove phrases such as AUTHORITATIVE GUIDANCE and MANDATORY COMPLIANCE. State that the skill provides optional troubleshooting guidance that must follow user and platform instructions.

remediation.issue: Production change examples appear near diagnostic guidance
remediation.suggestion: Label every mutating Azure CLI or kubectl command as approval-required, and separate read-only checks from remediation commands.

remediation.issue: Environment variable examples triggered sensitive-access scanners
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that AZURE_CLIENT_ID is an identifier, avoid printing environment values, and prefer managed identity examples without secret-like variable names.

content.value_statement: Azure incidents can span services, logs, identity, and networking. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured Azure troubleshooting paths.
actual_capabilities: Guides Azure triage through resource health, activity logs, metrics, logs, and recent changes.
Provides App Service diagnostics for CPU, deployments, crashes, slow responses, TLS, and health checks.
Covers Container Apps and Functions checks for image pulls, cold starts, ports, logs, and App Insights.
Routes AKS incidents to playbooks for nodes, pods, networking, DNS, upgrades, and scheduling.
Includes Event Hubs and Service Bus troubleshooting for authentication, AMQP, locks, retries, and checkpointing.
Provides KQL and Azure CLI examples with placeholders for user-owned resources.
limitations: Does not replace Azure support, service health advisories, or incident response procedures.
Requires valid Azure context, permissions, and resource identifiers for live diagnostics.
Some examples can change Azure resources and need explicit user approval before use.
Guidance may need adaptation for private networks, custom policies, or regulated environments.

use_cases.title: Triage App Service outages
use_cases.description: Investigate high CPU, deployment failures, crashes, slow responses, TLS issues, and failed health checks.

use_cases.title: Resolve AKS workload failures
use_cases.description: Collect evidence for unreachable clusters, unhealthy nodes, pending pods, crash loops, DNS failures, and ingress issues.

use_cases.title: Debug Azure messaging clients
use_cases.description: Analyze Event Hubs and Service Bus authentication, connectivity, retry, checkpointing, and lock-loss problems.

prompt_templates.title: Check resource health
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for one Azure resource.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me diagnose an Azure resource issue. Start with resource health, recent activity, metrics, and logs. Ask for any missing resource identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate App Service errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Troubleshoot my App Service issue. The symptoms are: <symptoms>. Guide me through safe read-only checks before any remediation.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze an AKS incident
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate this AKS problem: <symptom>. Use Azure-side evidence first, then Kubernetes evidence. Separate read-only checks from change operations.

prompt_templates.title: Correlate messaging failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced Event Hubs or Service Bus incident analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Azure messaging outage across SDK errors, authentication, network paths, retry settings, and recent changes. Provide root cause confidence and next checks.

output_examples.input: App Service started returning 503 after the latest deployment.
output_examples.output: The response should rank deployment history, startup logs, health-check configuration, and recent activity. It should separate evidence from likely cause.

output_examples.input: AKS pods are Pending in one namespace.
output_examples.output: The response should check events, quotas, node capacity, taints, PVC status, and scheduler signals before suggesting remediation.

output_examples.input: Service Bus receivers keep losing message locks.
output_examples.output: The response should inspect processing time, auto-renewal, transient link detach, retry policy, and SDK usage patterns.

best_practices: Start with read-only evidence before suggesting changes to production resources.
Ask for subscription, resource group, resource name, time window, and recent changes when missing.
Quote the evidence that supports any root-cause claim and state confidence clearly.
anti_patterns: Do not run mutating Azure CLI or kubectl commands without explicit approval.
Do not assume the first warning is the root cause without correlating logs and metrics.
Do not expose secrets, connection strings, or full environment dumps during troubleshooting.

faq.question: Which Azure services does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers App Service, Container Apps, Functions, AKS, Event Hubs, Service Bus, Azure Monitor, AppLens, and resource health.

faq.question: Can it run Azure commands for me?
faq.answer: It provides command guidance and tool paths. Live commands require the client tools, Azure permissions, and user approval for changes.

faq.question: Does it support AKS troubleshooting?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes playbooks for cluster access, nodes, pods, kube-system, ingress, DNS, networking, scheduling, and upgrades.

faq.question: Can it help with Azure messaging SDK errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Event Hubs and Service Bus errors, authentication, AMQP connectivity, retry settings, checkpointing, and lock issues.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the service, resource identifiers, symptom, time window, impact, recent changes, and any relevant error messages.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for Azure support?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure diagnostics and remediation planning, but service outages and severe incidents may still need Azure support.
